mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over a 3-month window signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the predicted negative returns are not statistically distinguishable from zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with reduced corporate earnings expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY growth < -2% for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not significantly below zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 7% for three consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand and profit pressure, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered months, or the predicted negative effect is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower during triggered periods compared to baseline, or the rank IC falls below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below 1.5% over a 6-month window signals a disinflationary tightening, which historically precedes equity market drawdowns, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases while CPIAUCSL < 1.5% for 6 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the predicted negative effect is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) and a decline in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over a 3-month window signals a precautionary savings regime that depresses near-term demand and equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS rises while GDPC1 falls for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower during triggered periods, or the rank IC is below 0.04.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 6% combined with a decline in average hourly earnings (implied by PAYEMS and UNRATE dynamics) over a 6-month window signals deteriorating labor cost conditions, which historically precede negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 6.0% and PAYEMS growth < 0.5% for 6 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods, or the predicted effect is not robust across at least two business cycle episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for 12 consecutive months signals a housing market recovery that boosts consumer confidence and spending, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher during periods of sustained above-trend housing starts, or the rank IC falls below 0.06.
